info.title: MyParcel API
info.summary: API that provides endpoints to integrate with the MyParcel platform.
info.description: Allows MyParcel users to query delivery options, pickup & drop off locations with opening hours, register & trace shipments, print labels and more.

/.description: Reports the status of the API.

get.description:
Get the delivery options for a given location and carrier.

If none of the optional parameters are specified then the following
default will be used: If a request is made for the delivery options
between Friday after the default cutoff_time (15:30) and Monday before
the default cutoff_time (15:30) then Tuesday will be shown as the next
possible delivery date.
Use this endpoint to receive a list of nearby drop off points, where shipments can be dropped off upon shipping. Results are ordered by distance from the provided postal code or coordinates.

post.description: This endpoint is often used by external parties to facilitate return shipments on a dedicated part of their website, mainly when offering reverse logistics e.g. repair services. It will allow the consumer to send packages to the merchant directly from the merchant's website.

404.description: If this option is not enables then `HTTP 404 Not Found` is returned.

get.summary: Gets a list of Shipments, optionally filtered using parameters.
get.description: This operation returns a list of Shipments available to this User.

post.description: Add shipments allows you to create standard and related return shipments.

put.description: This operation can be used to update certain fields of a shipment. The fields that can be modified depend on the status of the shipment.

200.description: Shipment update was successful. Returns full shipments when Accept version 1.2 is used.

patch.description:
Partially update shipments. This operation can be used to update the
hidden, status, or delivered fields of one or more shipments.

The status is only accepted as an actual state change when cancelling a
Trunkrs shipment: the shipment must still be in the Pending - Registered
status and within its cancellation window. For every other carrier the
status must match the current status of the shipment.

get.description: Get shipments by id. A maximum of 100 shipment IDs can be requested at once.

delete.description:
This operation can be used to delete shipments for which a label has not yet been created.
However, outside of housekeeping, this is not really necessary since Shipments not handed over to the distributor will not be billed by MyParcel; thus unused shipments which are not deleted have no financial consequences.

get.description:
#### Get Shipment labels
You can specify label format and positions of labels on the first page with the
__format__ and __positions__ query parameters. The __positions__ query only works when you specify the A4 format
and is only applied on the first page with labels. Accounts with __Post-payment__ payment methods can fetch
multiple labels in one call. For accounts with __Pre-payment__ payment method an `HTTP 402 Payment Required`
with a PaymentInstructions object is returned if the label has not been paid for yet.

##### Multi-collo shipments
When a label for a multi collo shipment is requested, labels for all shipments parts of the multi collo shipment
will be generated. Each shipment within a multi collo shipment MUST be labeled with a specific label containing
a unique barcode.

2XX.description:
##### Shipment Label Response
Contains one or more shipment labels in the desired media format.

###### Asynchronous retrieval of labels
When retrieving multiple pages worth of labels, it is recommended to perform an async request by defining
the `Accept` header `application/vnd.shipment_label_link+json`. The response will then contain a promise
URL to the desired label(s). These promise URLs will return `HTTP 404 Not Found` until they're ready.
Depending on the number of labels, this process will take between 3 seconds and 3 minutes. You can regularly
check whether the label is available or you can use the `label_created` webhooks.

##### ZPL labels
Currently, our system supports only PostNL and Bpost labels in ZPL format for the following shipment types:
  - Domestic shipments for both normal packages and mailbox packages.
  - EU shipments

If you request a rest of world label, the system will return a label in PDF format. Additionally, you can
request just one label at a time.

For Bpost shipments, you can request a label in ZPL format only if you have not requested a PDF label
before. After you requested a ZPL label, you can also request a PDF label.

bad_request.description:
The request could not be understood by the server due to malformed
syntax. The client should not repeat the request without modifications.

client_error.description:
Client-side error response. The representation is selected via
standard HTTP content negotiation on the `Accept` header.

- **Default:** when the caller does **not** list
  `application/problem+json` in `Accept`, the response is returned
  with `Content-Type: application/json` and the legacy MyParcel
  error envelope (`{ message, request_id, status_code, errors[] }`).
- **Opt-in:** when the caller lists `application/problem+json` in
  `Accept`, the response is returned with
  `Content-Type: application/problem+json` and the RFC 9457
  problem-detail document (the fields from section 3.1).
  Sub-errors carry a JSON Pointer in `instance` and a narrowed
  `type` URI derived from the error code.

direct_printing_no_active_subscription.description: Direct printing requires an active subscription.

download_url.description: This is the download URL object.

drop_off_points.description: A collection of Drop Off Points.

empty.description: This response is given when the request is successful and the response is empty.

invalid_content_type.description: This response is given when the request Content-Type is not supported.

invalid_content_type_or_problem.description:
This response is given when the request Content-Type is not supported.

The representation is selected via standard HTTP content negotiation
on the `Accept` header. By default the legacy MyParcel error envelope
is returned with `Content-Type: application/json`. When the caller
lists `application/problem+json` in `Accept`, the response is returned
with `Content-Type: application/problem+json` and the RFC 9457
problem-detail document instead.

not_found.description:
The requested resource could not be found or its existence may not be
disclosed. This may be temporary or permanent.

permission_denied.description:
No credentials have been sent with the request, or the wrong credentials are sent. Tip: check if the API key
is properly attached in the header:

```http
Authorization: bearer BASE64_ENCODED_API_KEY
```

server_error.description:
Server-side error response. The representation is selected via
standard HTTP content negotiation on the `Accept` header.

- **Default:** when the caller does **not** list
  `application/problem+json` in `Accept`, the legacy MyParcel
  system-error envelope is returned with
  `Content-Type: application/json`.
- **Opt-in:** when the caller lists `application/problem+json` in
  `Accept`, the response is returned with
  `Content-Type: application/problem+json` and the RFC 9457
  problem-detail document. Internal error codes are not included
  in the type URI. A 5xx response on this path uses
  `type: urn:problem:server-error`.

shipment_validation_error.description:
This response is given when one or more shipments are invalid, e.g.
because a shipment doesn't exist, contains changes that aren't allowed,
or fails the carrier's validation. The errors identify the invalid
shipments.

cutoff_time.name: cutoff_time
cutoff_time.description: This option allows the **Merchant** to indicate the latest cutoff time before which a consumer order will still be picked, packed and dispatched on the same/first set drop-off day, taking into account the drop-off delay. Default time is 15:30. For example, if cutoff time is 15:30, Monday is a delivery day and there's no delivery delay; all orders placed Monday before 15:30 will be dropped of at PostNL on that same Monday in time for the Monday collection.

delayed.name: delayed
delayed.description: Filter on whether the current event code means the shipment has been delayed.

delivery_date.name: delivery_date
delivery_date.description: The date on which the package has to be delivered.

delivery_time.name: delivery_time
delivery_time.description:
The time on which a package has to be delivered.
> __Note__: This is only an indication of time the package will be
>           delivered on the selected date.

delivery_options_package_type.name: package_type
delivery_options_package_type.description:
Package type to get the delivery options for. When omitted a
carrier-specific default is used.

delivery_type.name: delivery_type
delivery_type.description: Delivery type to get the delivery options for.

deliverydays_window.name: deliverydays_window
deliverydays_window.description: This options allows the Merchant to set the number of days into the future for which they want to show their consumers delivery options. For example, if set to 3 in their check-out, a consumer ordering on Monday will see possible delivery options for Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday (provided there is no drop-off delay, it's before the cutoff time, and they go to PostNL on Mondays).

distance.name: distance
distance.description: Provide the radius in kilometers for which you want to find drop off points. The default distance differs by carrier.

dropoff_days.name: dropoff_days
dropoff_days.description: This options allows the **Merchant** to set the days she normally goes to PostNL to hand in her parcels. By default Saturday and Sunday are excluded.

dropoff_delay.name: dropoff_delay
dropoff_delay.description: This options allows the **Merchant** to set the number of days it takes them to pick, pack and hand in their parcels at the carrier when ordered before the cutoff time. The default value is 0.

dropoff_today.name: dropoff_today
dropoff_today.description: Use this parameter to only show Shipments that need to be dropped off today.

exclude_delivery_type.name: exclude_delivery_type
exclude_delivery_type.description: Exclude shipments with a specific delivery type. This parameter can be used multiple times to exclude multiple delivery types.

exclude_parcel_lockers.name: exclude_parcel_lockers
exclude_parcel_lockers.description: This option allows to filter out pickup locations that are parcel lockers.

format.name: format
format.description:
The paper size of the PDF as specified in ISO216. Currently, A4 and A6 are supported. When A4 is chosen you
can specify the label positions. When requesting the label for a shipment that contains a custom form, you can
only request an A4 format.

Currently only `price` is supported.

Whether to include secondary (multicollo child) Shipments in the results.
Pass `1` to include them; `0` (the default) excludes them.

latitude.name: latitude

limit.name: limit

longitude.name: longitude
longitude.description: This provides the ability to search locations through the coordinates. If only longitude is provided without latitude, it will be ignored.

monday_delivery.name: monday_delivery
monday_delivery.description:
Monday delivery is only possible when the package is delivered before
15.00 on Saturday at the designated PostNL locations.
> __Note__: To activate Monday delivery, value 6 must be given with
> [dropoff_days], value 1 must be given by [monday_delivery]. And on
> Saturday the [cutoff_time] must be before 15:00 (14:30 recommended)
> so that Monday will be shown.

positions.name: positions

The positions of the label on an A4 sheet. A position is identified by a digit from `1` to `4`. You can specify
up to four positions separated by semicolons (`;`) or commas (`,`).

__Note__: This parameter only works when you specify the `A4` __format__ and only applies to the first page
when requesting multiple pages worth of labels. Subsequent pages use the default positioning `1;2;3;4`.

common_responses_problem.title: Problem Details (RFC 9457)
common_responses_problem.description: RFC 9457 problem-detail object returned when the caller lists `application/problem+json` in the Accept header. Top-level fields are strictly the five defined in RFC 9457 §3.1; the `errors` array is an extension populated when the underlying exception carried per-field validator errors.

type.description: URI reference identifying the problem type. Derived from the error code (e.g. `urn:problem:invalid-shipments`) or, when no matching code exists, a status-based fallback URN.

title.description: A short, human-readable summary of the problem type.

status.description: The HTTP status code for this occurrence.

detail.description: A human-readable explanation specific to this occurrence.

instance.description: URI reference identifying the specific occurrence. The request path for the top-level object; the RFC 6901 JSON Pointer of the failing field for each `errors[]` entry.

request_id.description: Per-request correlation identifier. Mirrors the value of the `X-Request-Id` response header and the legacy envelope's `request_id` field. Allowed as an RFC 9457 §3.2 extension member so consumers don't have to read both header and body for tracing.

errors.description: Sub-problem list. Each entry is itself an RFC 9457 problem-detail object describing one failing field. The sub-error `type`/`title` narrow past the wrapping problem when the underlying error code maps to a more specific type (e.g. `urn:problem:invalid-address`, `urn:problem:invalid-physical-properties`).

carrier_active.description: Whether the carrier of the shipment is active for the shop the shipment was created with. Only present in paginated responses, i.e. those of `GET /shipments` and `GET /shipments/{ids}`.

common_defs_date_and_time.title: common.defs.DateAndTime
common_defs_date_and_time.description:
Represents a date in ISO 8601 format and a time in ISO 8601 format, separated
by a space, so:

```
YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss.u
```

Where:
  - `YYYY` represents a four-digit year, `0000` through `9999`
  - `MM` represents a zero-padded month of the year, `01` through `12`
  - `DD` represents a zero-padded day of that month, `01` through `31`
and:
  - `hh` represents a zero-padded hour, `00` through `24`
  - `mm` represents a zero-padded minute, `00` through `59`
  - `ss` (optional) represents a zero-padded second, `00` through `60`
    (where `60` is only used to denote an added leap second)
  - `.u` (optional) represents a fraction of a second, `.0` through `.999999+`

common_defs_date.title: common.defs.Date
common_defs_date.description:
Represents a date in ISO 8601 format:

```
YYYY-MM-DD
```

Where:
  - `YYYY` represents a four-digit year, `0000` through `9999`
  - `MM` represents a zero-padded month of the year, `01` through `12`
  - `DD` represents a zero-padded day of that month, `01` through `31`

common_defs_time.title: common.defs.Time
common_defs_time.description:
Represents a time in ISO 8601 format:

```
hh:mm:ss.u
```

Where:
  - `hh` represents a zero-padded hour, `00` through `24`
  - `mm` represents a zero-padded minute, `00` through `59`
  - `ss` (optional) represents a zero-padded second, `00` through `60`
    (where `60` is only used to denote an added leap second)
  - `.u` (optional) represents a fraction of a second, `.0` through `.999999+`
